key_insight: HamGNN-NEGF uses an E(3)-equivariant graph neural network to predict DFT-quality Hamiltonians, enabling linear-scaling quantum transport for device-scale systems.
engineering_relevance: It makes predictive quantum transport feasible for realistic nanoelectronic devices with thousands of atoms, while retaining near-DFT accuracy and drastically reducing computational cost.
method: Train on small-structure DFT Hamiltonians, then predict Hamiltonians for larger devices.
Combine predicted Hamiltonians with DFT electrode self-energies, nonorthogonal KPM for Fermi-level finding, and recursive Green's function transport.
Bypass transport self-consistency to enable faster calculations, including HSE06 and weakly nonlinear finite-bias cases.
evidence_signal: Benchmarks on Pt-Si-Pt, Pt-Si:P-Pt, and Pt-molecule-Pt junctions report meV-level Hamiltonian accuracy, faithful transmission spectra, and simulations beyond 10,000 atoms with >1000x speedups for sub-500-atom devices.
watch_item: The zero-bias Hamiltonian approximation may be less reliable for strongly nonlinear or high-bias transport regimes.
paper_title: Linear-Scaling Quantum Transport from Machine-Learning Density Functional Theory Hamiltonians
